classification.difficultyReason: Complete the square, including factoring out a negative leading coefficient, then interpret the vertex form as horizontal and vertical shifts and construct each sketch. Finding exact intercepts and recognising when no real intercepts exist link routine algebra with graphical features; the method is explicitly supplied.

content.prompt: In each part, complete the square in the quadratic. Then identify its graph as a translation of either $y=x^2$ or $y=-x^2$. Finally, sketch its graph.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}y&=x^2+2x+1-1+3\\y&=(x+1)^2+2\end{align*}$$
The graph of $y=x^2$ shifts left 1 and up 2. Its vertex is $(-1,2)$, its axis of symmetry is $x=-1$, and its $y$-intercept is $3$. There are no $x$-intercepts.

spec.description: Upward parabola with vertex, symmetry guide, marked point and labelled y-intercept.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}y&=x^2-2x+1-1-2\\y&=(x-1)^2-3\end{align*}$$
The graph of $y=x^2$ shifts right 1 and down 3. The vertex is $(1,-3)$ and the $y$-intercept is $-2$.
$$\begin{align*}(x-1)^2&=3\\x&=1\pm\sqrt3\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Upward parabola with vertex and exact intercept labels.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}y&=-(x^2-4x)+1\\y&=-\big((x-2)^2-4\big)+1\\y&=-(x-2)^2+5\end{align*}$$
The graph of $y=-x^2$ shifts right 2 and up 5. The vertex is $(2,5)$ and the $y$-intercept is $1$.
$$\begin{align*}(x-2)^2&=5\\x&=2\pm\sqrt5\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Downward parabola with vertex, y-intercept and exact roots. A leader separates the small negative root label from the y-axis.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}y&=-(x^2+4x)-5\\y&=-\big((x+2)^2-4\big)-5\\y&=-(x+2)^2-1\end{align*}$$
The graph of $y=-x^2$ shifts left 2 and down 1. Its vertex is $(-2,-1)$, its axis of symmetry is $x=-2$, and its $y$-intercept is $-5$. There are no $x$-intercepts.

spec.description: Downward parabola below the x-axis, with symmetry guide and the two source-marked points.
